The island is close to the northern tip of Hinchinbrook Island off the coast from Cardwell in Rockingham Bay and is part of the Great Barrier Reef World Heritage Area.
Covering 8.3 square kilometres (3.2 sq mi), the island is located 17 kilometres (10.6 mi) from shore. It is covered mostly with open eucalypt forest, rainforested gullies and semi permanent creek water.


== History ==
For many thousands of years before non-indigenous peoples arrived in the region, Goold, neighbouring islands, and surrounding seas were occupied, used, and enjoyed by generations of the Bandjin peoples' ancestors, leaving behind an array of stone fish traps and shell middens which can still be found on and around the island to this day.

One of the earliest European accounts of Aboriginal Peoples at Goold Island is provided by  Phillip Park King who in 1818 entered Rockingham Bay as part of survey of the 'intertropical and western coasts of Australia'.
